repos.head: 1ec1784

findings.title: Slice exemption lets psql interpolation through (whitespace before colon; -v variables)
findings.problem: The blanking regex (\w)\s*:\s*(?=\w) inside any [...] span accepts `[ x :v ]` and `a[1:n]` where psql still substitutes :v / :n. `psql -v n=... -c 'select a[1:n] from t'` is allowed; -v is not refused. Substituted text can close the slice and append SQL the analyzer never saw.
findings.rootCause: A static check cannot tell a slice from a variable reference (psql lexes :name everywhere outside quotes), and the exemption trusts any bracket span and tolerates whitespace.
findings.fix: Fixed on the branch after this review: the exemption is limited to integer bounds ([2:3]); a bound that is a name stays refused; -v, --set and --variable are refused; the adversarial rows are in the test.

findings.title: Tests lack adversarial rows for the new regex
findings.problem: No rows for a[x :v], -v with a slice, nested brackets, a[1::n], an unclosed [, or a slice followed by '; select :v'.
findings.rootCause: Only the cases listed in the spec were written.
findings.fix: Added on the branch after this review: [ x :v ], a nested a[b[1:2]:n], a[1:2]; select :v, and the four -v spellings.

tdd.notes: Behavior tests through analyze, no mocks, cases match the spec, test-first claimed in the commit message but not independently verifiable. Missing adversarial and regression rows around the new regex (added after the review).
